question: As per Article 53 of the Constitution of India, with whom are all the executive powers of the Union vested?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• As per Article 53 of the Constitution of India, **all the executive powers of the Union are vested in the President.**
 
• The President of India is the supreme commander of the defense forces of India and exercises executive powers either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
• The President's executive powers are exercised in accordance with the Constitution and laws made by Parliament.
 
• The President also has the power to appoint the Prime Minister and other ministers, who assist in the administration of the Union government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
 
• The executive powers of the President are exercised in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
